title: Past Perfect & Past Perfect Continuous
subtitle: Add duration to your storytelling: how long something had been happening before another past event.
objectives: Review the past perfect (had + past participle)
Form and use the past perfect continuous (had been + -ing)
Choose between them based on result vs. duration, just like present perfect vs. continuous

content.intro: The past perfect continuous does for the past what the present perfect continuous does for the present — it adds a sense of ongoing duration before another past moment.

rules.heading: a) Past perfect (review)
rules.body:
had + past participle = the earlier of two past events, focused on the result.

  • She had finished the report before the meeting.

rules.heading: b) Past perfect continuous
rules.body:
had been + -ing = emphasizes the duration of an activity happening before another past moment.

  • She had been working on the report for hours before the meeting. (the activity, and how long)
  • He was tired because he had been running.

examples: She had finished the report before the meeting.
She had been working on the report for hours before the meeting.
He was tired because he had been running.
They had been waiting for an hour when the bus finally came.
I had already eaten when they arrived.
We had been driving for six hours before we stopped.

commonMistakes.wrong: He was tired because he had run for an hour. (emphasizing the ongoing activity)
commonMistakes.right: He was tired because he had been running for an hour.
commonMistakes.why: Emphasizing the duration/activity that caused the tiredness needs the past perfect continuous.

commonMistakes.wrong: They had been wait for an hour.
commonMistakes.right: They had been waiting for an hour.
commonMistakes.why: The continuous form needs the -ing verb, not the base form.

commonMistakes.wrong: I had ate already when they arrived.
commonMistakes.right: I had already eaten when they arrived.
commonMistakes.why: The past perfect needs the past participle (eaten), not the simple past form (ate).

items.prompt: She ___ (finish) the report before the meeting.

items.explanation: Emphasizing the duration of the activity — past perfect continuous.

items.prompt: They ___ (wait) for an hour when the bus came.
items.explanation: Duration before another past event — past perfect continuous.

items.prompt: We ___ for six hours before we stopped.
items.explanation: Emphasis on the ongoing duration — past perfect continuous.
A completed result before another past event — past perfect (simple).

items.incorrect: They had been wait for an hour.
answer: They had been waiting for an hour.
items.explanation: The continuous form needs the -ing verb.

items.incorrect: She had been finish the report.
items.explanation: A completed result needs the past perfect simple, not the continuous, and "finish" needs the past participle.

summary: Past perfect (had + past participle) = result, the earlier of two past events.
Past perfect continuous (had been + -ing) = duration/activity before another past moment.
Same logic as present perfect vs. continuous, just shifted one step further into the past.
